profile_text.body:
Meta is a public company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, traded on public markets under the ticker META. Its website positions the company as a platform for AI developers, describing tools and models that developers can build on. The site highlights the Meta Model API as a central access point, noting compatibility with existing OpenAI SDK clients and a quick-start path to a first working request in under five minutes.

The company's primary AI product tracked here is Llama, an open-weight model family that is often self-hosted, available at llama.com. The site also describes Muse Spark, which it characterizes as optimized for coding tasks including writing, reviewing, and shipping code with fewer steps and lower latency, and as competitive for building coding agents and review bots. Muse Image is presented as a reasoning model that plans layout before drawing and is offered through the Meta Model API at $0.01 per image. The site additionally describes multi-agent workflow capabilities allowing a single model to interact with a computer by clicking through applications and moving between interfaces.

Meta's most recently reported annual revenue was $200,966,000,000 for the period ending December 31, 2025, filed on a 10-K form. The company faces active litigation in federal court, including Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc. and Chicken Soup for the Soul, LLC v. Meta Platforms Inc., both in the Northern District of California, and Neural AI, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc. in the Western District of Texas. The held facts also record 175 instances of legal exposure associated with California. Several third-party MCP servers built around Meta's advertising infrastructure appear in the registry, covering Facebook and Instagram ad automation, campaign management, and performance analysis.
